notes: §1985:VII.2.12.4 GR1: "The RERUN clause specifies when and where the rerun information is recorded", a) in file-name-1 "on each reel or unit of an output file" and b) "as a separate file on a device specified by the implementor" when implementor-name is specified. Implemented at 85: the source side (rerunClause and rerunEvery parse the clause, VisitRerunClause is the edition arm, ScreenRerunClauses asks the syntax rules and tells GR1's two ways apart by the ON word) and, since kb/Work PB5198, the recording of way b for the integer-1 RECORDS form: RecordRerunRecords keeps the clause on file-name-2 (FileModel.RerunRecords), the emitter registers it on the connector (EmitRerunRegistration, CobolFile.RegisterRerunRecords) and FileConnector.RecordProcessed appends one line, RERUN, the file-name and the count since the OPEN, to the host file the implementor-name spells as an ASSIGN target spells one. Way a (rerun information on each reel or unit of an output file) belongs to the forms a, b and g of GR2, which the implementor need not provide (GR2: "at least one of the specified forms"); those forms are accepted and write nothing, docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.11. The witness runs RERUN ON implementor-name EVERY 2 RECORDS OF a sequential file and EVERY 1 RECORDS OF a relative file and reads the device back.

No 2023 clause carries the RERUN clause. The wording candidates cover DELETE, READ, OPEN, CLOSE and similar statements, none of them rerun information, so the clause is dropped.
